The premise of your question is false. In Switzerland, the general requirement for naturalization is 10 years of residence (for EU/EFTA citizens) or 12 years for non-EU/EFTA citizens, but this is calculated based on total residence in Switzerland with a valid permit, not specifically tied to a B permit alone. Additionally, naturalization requires meeting several other conditions, including integration, knowledge of the local language, and no serious legal issues.

Please note that immigration regulations can change, and individual circumstances may affect eligibility. For accurate, up-to-date information, consult the Swiss State Secretariat for Migration (SEM) or a legal expert in Swiss immigration law.
